task: Apply next_steps item 2 from decode-compiler-tree-lexer-cache-fix.json: make _incremental_sync genuinely incremental at the lex layer (re-lex only newly appended text on the common path) instead of re-lexing the full prefix through the cached lexer every call; prove I3/I6 (next_terminals()/accepts() and build_completion_forest coverage/n_paths) byte-identical at every step, not just the final one.

summary: New self._fed_last_token_start: int | None -- absolute offset into self._prefix where the last already-fed token starts; None before anything is fed. Reset in reset().
_full_sync now also records self._fed_last_token_start = tokens[fed_token_count-1].start_pos after a successful feed.

New shared helper _feed_delta_tokens(prefix, delta, keys, *, base_offset): factored feed-loop (same UnexpectedToken/UnexpectedEOF handling as before) that also updates self._fed_last_token_start from whichever delta token was last fed, at base_offset + tok.start_pos.

_incremental_sync: when self._fed_token_count > 0 and self._fed_last_token_start is not None, re-lex only prefix[safe_offset:] (the last fed token plus newly appended text) instead of the whole prefix. Compares the suffix's first token against the previously-fed boundary token; if unchanged, splices self._fed_tokens[:boundary_idx] onto the freshly-lexed suffix keys and feeds only the new tokens. Falls back to the exact pre-existing _full_sync(prefix) path on any lex failure, empty suffix-lex result, or a changed boundary-token identity (token still growing, e.g. NAME/COMPONENT gluing) -- never guesses.
No change to _full_sync/_sync external contract, probe_chunk (explicitly out of scope), or any grammar/terminal definition.
change.why_safe: Lark's BasicLexer is maximal-munch: a token that already ended before an unchanged character is permanently settled and cannot be reopened by appending text strictly after it -- only the LAST fed token (still live at end-of-string when it was lexed) can grow. self._fed_last_token_start anchors exactly that one uncertain token; re-lexing prefix[start:] re-derives it (and anything after it) exactly as a full relex would. Verified directly (not assumed): Token.start_pos/end_pos are populated by BasicLexer.next_token unconditionally, independent of propagate_positions (which only controls parse-tree metadata, a different Lark option) -- confirmed by reading lark/lexer.py and by direct .venv-diag REPL check. Also verified no terminal in openui.lark uses a lookbehind/\b-style regex assertion, which matters because LexerThread.from_text(lexer, suffix) lexes suffix as a fresh string (no left-context view into the original prefix).

known_limitation.growing_boundary_token: When the last-fed token itself keeps growing one character/byte at a time (e.g. advance('T'), advance('Te'), advance('Tex'), ... -- the DSL tokenizer's byte/char literal-content fallback channel, B: tokens), every such call still triggers a full _full_sync, identical cost to pre-fix. Not a regression (this is exactly what _incremental_sync already did for this case), but this fix provides no benefit there. The grammar-vocabulary path (whole COMPONENT/NAME/keyword pieces per advance() call, which is what build_completion_forest's witness search and _forward_binder_component_requirements predominantly exercise) is where this fix's benefit concentrates. See next_steps item 1 for the properly-scoped follow-up.

interpretation: Closes next_steps item 2 from decode-compiler-tree-lexer-cache-fix.json. The suffix-only relex is correct (I3/I6 proven at every step of a long incremental drive and at the build_completion_forest decode-output layer) and measurably reduces lex work: 2.97x fewer characters lexed / up to 2.56x wall time on a long growing prefix; 1.45-1.46x fewer characters / 1.09-1.49x wall time on the finding's own short prefixes. The gap between the two results is explained (short absolute branch lengths bounded by max_path_tokens<=8, plus a large unavoidable per-candidate full-lex cost this fix does not touch), not hidden.
scope_note: No train/eval run, no checkpoint, no --ship-gates scoreboard -- same tier as the rest of this PR chain. Does not help the growing-boundary-token case (see known_limitation). Slicing prefix[safe_offset:] into a fresh string relies on this grammar's terminals having no lookbehind/\b assertions -- verified true today, not enforced by a runtime check. probe_chunk is untouched (out of scope per task).
